title: Are Dinosaur Fossils Resting on the Moon?
description: Did the massive asteroid impact that wiped out the dinosaurs actually launch Earth rocks—and fossils—all the way to the Moon? Discover the incredible physics of hypervelocity ejecta! Could lunar missions find Earth's missing prehistory? 🦖🌕
script:
If you want to find the most pristine, perfectly preserved dinosaur fossils in existence, the best paleontological dig site in the solar system might not be in the deserts of Montana or Patagonia—it might actually be on the surface of the Moon.

Sixty-six million years ago, a colossal asteroid roughly ten to fifteen kilometers in diameter slammed into the Yucatán Peninsula at a blistering speed of 20 kilometers per second, creating what we now know as the Chicxulub crater. The energy unleashed by this catastrophic event was equivalent to over 100 million megatons of TNT, millions of times more powerful than the largest nuclear weapon ever detonated. While the thermal flash and subsequent global environmental catastrophe spelled doom for non-avian dinosaurs, the initial physics of the collision triggered a fascinating and bizarre astrophysical phenomenon known as spallation.

During a hypervelocity impact, shockwaves ripple through the target body with unimaginable pressure. Near the point of impact, the surface layer of Earth's crust was accelerated to speeds far exceeding Earth's escape velocity of 11.2 kilometers per second before the thermal energy could fully vaporize it. Billions of tons of terrestrial rock, topsoil, and organic debris were violently blasted straight through the atmosphere into outer space.

Computer simulations conducted by planetary scientists suggest that a small percentage of this terrestrial debris was launched onto ballistic trajectories that intercepted the Earth-Moon system. Over days and weeks following the impact, chunks of Cretaceous Earth—potentially containing pristine, un-weathered fragments of plants, marine organisms, and fossilized dinosaur remains—rained down onto the lunar surface.

Because the Moon lacks an atmosphere, tectonic activity, liquid water, or organic decomposition, any terrestrial ejecta that survived a low-velocity impact on the lunar surface was preserved in a near-permanent, sterile deep freeze. On Earth, plate tectonics, wind, and water erosion continuously erase the geological record over millions of years. On the Moon, however, these displaced pieces of ancient Earth remain essentially pristine time capsules, locked within the vacuum of space for 66 million years.

When future astronauts return to the Moon to mine and study lunar regolith, they may not just be uncovering alien rocks—they could very well unearth Earth's lost prehistory, finding genuine Cretaceous fossils sitting silently in the dust of another world.

chosen_topic: When the massive asteroid struck Earth 66 million years ago and wiped out the dinosaurs, the impact was so violent that tons of terrestrial rock were blasted into outer space, meaning genuine pieces of Earth containing dinosaur fossils might actually be resting on the Moon.
